full_judgment:
7. The heirs of Jahir Ali that is Md Manik Mia and Mst. Sabiya Begum the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 14 of 1994/93 of 1994 who are the defendant Nos.1 and 2 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 in brief their case is that Raman Ram Malakar, Gagan Ram Malakar and Ador Ram Malakar were owners of the first schedule land and while possessing the first schedule land Raman Ram Malakar and his two aforesaid brothers sold the first schedule land to Jahir Ali, (the predecessor of the plaintiffs) on 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11 Baisakh 1359 BS through a saf kabala. After getting the scheduled land they paid rent regularly to Zamidar. While possessing the first schedule land, Jahir Ali Sold 0.33 acres of land out of the land as described in first schedule land to Abdur Rahman (the predecessor of 4-12 defendants), the defendant Nos.1-3 on different dates by saf kabala and Jahir Ali has been possessing the remaining 0.07 acres of land by constructing tin shed building where made a tea-stall for long years. Subsequently, he died leaving behind the plaintiff No.1 as son and the plaintiff No. 2 as daughter. Later on the aforesaid Md Manik Mia and Mst Sabiya Begum came to know that on 24-4-1952 Gagan Ram Malakar and his two brothers executed a sale deed, in respect of suit land in favour of Jahir Ali who also executed ekrarnama (deed of agreement) promising to recovery the land to the vendors on repayment of the consideration money within 30th Chaitra 1361 BS corresponding to 24-4-1946. The plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by running tea-stall. The defendant Nos. 4-12 recently started construction a new building in first schedule of the plaint and threatened the defendants to destroy their restaurant from the suit land. In the meantime the defendants through Daroga of local thana on 8-5-1994 issued a notice alleging that the plaintiffs are illegal possessor and the plaintiffs are restraining the defendant No.4 from constructing. After getting the said notice the plaintiffs requested the defendant No. 4 on 9-5-1994 for partition in respect of 0.07 acres. But the defendant No. 4 refused the request. The plaintiffs have been possessing the second schedule land which is included of first schedule for more than 12 years of the statutory period since their predecessors. But the land of second schedule was inadvertently recorded in the name of the defendant No.14 in separate khatian and Mouja. The plaintiffs came to know on first part of January, 1994 that 0.34 acres of first schedule was recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs on RS Dag No. 2771 of RS Khatian No. 557. Since the defendant No.14 in collusion of defendant No. 4 refused the title of the plaintiffs, it clouded the right, title and interest of the plaintiff. Hence, the plaintiffs constrained to file the instant suit. 

 10. The case of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 in brief, is that the predecessor of the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendants Charan Ram Malakar were owners of the first schedule land as described in schedule to the plaint. Subsequently, the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendants became successive owners by inheritance, Gagan Ram and his 2 brothers, predecessor of the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendant Nos. 9-10 during their life time produced CS Khatian and other documents before the employee of settlement Jarip at the time of preparation of SA Khatian. They believed SA Khatian was prepared in their names. The predecessors of the plaintiffs for their convenience of enjoyment partitioned the suit land along with other lands and accordingly Gagan Ram Malakar got the suit land in his saham. The plaintiffs filled up the suit land with earth. But the defendant Nos. 3-8 evicted the plaintiffs from the suit second schedule land by constructing tin shed building. The plaintiff on several times requested the defendant Nos.3-8 to leave the suit second schedule land in their favour. But the defendants claimed that the land of second schedule was recorded in the name of Government and they took lease from the Government. On searching in the local Tahsil Office, the plaintiffs came to know on 18-2-2014 that the land of first schedule of plaint was recorded in SA Khatian as canal খাল which was incorrect. In fact the suit land should be recorded as সাইলউরা in CS Khatian in the name of predecessor of the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendants. Thus the plaintiffs were cons-trained to file the suit for declaration of title by adverse possession for statutory period of 12 years in respect of first schedule land, decla-ration that SA Khatian is wrong in respect of first schedule land and Khas possession in respect of second schedule land as described in schedule to plaint. 

 23. Mr Dider Alam Kollol, the learned Advocate on behalf of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 of Transfer Appeal No. 2 of 2014 argued that the learned trial court without considering the evidence of the plaintiff appellants reached into erroneous decision. CS Khatian was filed by the original owner Charan Ram Malakar which was marked as Exhibit-1. But the learned court erroneously found that the plaintiff could not file documents in his support. In the plaint it was specifically mentioned that the plaintiffs were evicted by the defendants on first part of poush in 1400 BS. But the court below did not consider it. He finally submits the trial court in its judgment did not mention about the commissioners report which is totally misconceived on law. He also argued that learned court below on misconception of law found the deed in question dated 24-4-1952 is a mortgage deed. In fact that deed is within the mischief of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act but it was not alive at the date of commencement of Presidents Order No. 88 of 1972 on 3-8-1972. So, the said transaction does not attract section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Jahir Ali became owner on the basis of deed No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 and subsequently after selling the property 0.7 decimals remain with Jahir Ali. After death of Jahir Ali his heirs the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 and plaintiff of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 became owner and they are entitled for partition of 0.7 decimals of land.
